content.text: What is the latest news about Azure AI today?

Below is a detailed, thoroughly sourced update on the *latest* Azure AI–related developments as of **Wednesday, July 15, 2026** (today). The information draws on officially published Azure updates, Microsoft Build announcements, and industry coverage.

---

###  Azure Updates – July 15, 2026

As of today (July 15, 2026), new Azure features and releases have been captured in Microsoft’s Azure Updates feed, which consolidates official product news.

- **Document PII NextGen Playground (General Availability)**  
  The *Document PII NextGen Playground* within **Azure AI Language**, part of Microsoft Foundry, has entered general availability on July 1, 2026. This feature enables users to experiment with detecting and handling personally identifiable information (PII) within documents in a NextGen sandbox environment ([azure.microsoft.com](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/updates/)).

- **Recent Announcements (July 15, 2026)**  
  On **July 15, 2026**, the Azure updates feed lists several notable entries:
  - *Advanced platform metrics in Azure Monitor* entered *Public Preview*, offering enhanced observability for Azure infrastructure and services ([azurecharts.com](https://azurecharts.com/updates?monthback=0)).
  - A new *DevUI Agent Inspector* for the Microsoft Agent Framework was announced, improving development tooling for Azure-based AI agents ([azurecharts.com](https://azurecharts.com/updates?monthback=0)).

---

###  Microsoft Build 2026 & Azure AI Developments

Many of today’s Azure AI-related features stem from announcements at **Microsoft Build 2026**, which occurred earlier this summer.

#### Highlights include:

- **Microsoft Agent Platform & Foundry ecosystem**  
  - *Microsoft IQ*, *Foundry IQ*, *Work IQ*, and *Web IQ* were introduced as context layers empowering AI agents with internal and external enterprise knowledge. These platforms are now generally available ([aguidetocloud.com](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/blog/microsoft-build-2026-recap/)).  
  - The *Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0* (Python + .NET) is generally available, enabling developers to build, debug, and deploy AI agents within Azure Foundry ([aguidetocloud.com](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/blog/microsoft-build-2026-recap/)).

- **AI Models and Capabilities**
  - MAI‑Thinking‑1, a 35-billion‑parameter reasoning and code generation model with an expansive 256K context window, is now available in private preview via Microsoft Foundry ([github.com](https://github.com/microsoft/Build26-news/blob/main/news.md)).  
  - A family of seven new MAI models was announced, advancing Microsoft’s frontier AI ecosystem ([microsoft.ai](https://microsoft.ai/news/building-a-hillclimbing-machine-launching-seven-new-mai-models/)).  
  - Additional models such as MAI‑Image‑2.5, MAI‑Transcribe 1.5, MAI‑Voice‑2, and MAI‑Code‑1 were introduced and integrated across platforms including PowerPoint, OneDrive, Foundry, Copilot, and VS Code ([github.com](https://github.com/microsoft/Build26-news/blob/main/news.md)).

- **Supporting Infrastructure**
  - *Azure HorizonDB*, a high-performance PostgreSQL-compatible service designed for AI workloads, entered public preview at Build 2026 ([github.com](https://github.com/microsoft/Build26-news/blob/main/news.md)).  
  - *Project Rayfin* (BaaS for Microsoft Fabric) and Replit integration were revealed, enabling seamless transition from development prototype to governed production deployments ([github.com](https://github.com/microsoft/Build26-news/blob/main/news.md)).  
  - *Agent Control Specification (ACS)*, *Agent 365*, *Web IQ*, and other governance layers were introduced or made generally available, supporting agent governance, evaluation, publishing, and contextual deployment across Microsoft platforms ([aguidetocloud.com](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/blog/microsoft-build-2026-recap/)).

---

###  Context & Security in Azure AI Agents

- A **July 2026 edition** of the *Azure Database Security Newsletter* focuses on how the rise of AI agents requires evolution in database identity, access, monitoring, and protection strategies ([techcommunity.microsoft.com](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/coreinfrastructureandsecurityblog/azure-database-security-newsletter---july-2026/4534477)).  
- This underscores Microsoft’s emphasis not just on delivering AI agent functionality, but also securing and governing these new paradigms in enterprise environments.

---

###  Summary: What’s New Today

To summarize the most relevant **new and available** Azure AI offerings on **July 15, 2026**:

1. **Document PII NextGen Playground** – GA on Azure AI Language (part of Foundry).  
2. **Advanced platform metrics in Azure Monitor** – Entered Public Preview.  
3. **DevUI Agent Inspector** – Announced for the Microsoft Agent Framework.  
4. Build‑era releases now in GA or preview (from Build 2026):
   - Contextual intelligence services (*IQ suites*)
   - Agent tooling (Agent Framework 1.0, ACS, Agent 365)
   - MAI model family (Thinking‑1, Image‑2.5, Voice‑2, Transcribe 1.5, Code‑1)
   - Azure HorizonDB (PostgreSQL for AI)
   - Project Rayfin and integration pipelines (Replit, Fabric)

---

###  Key Dates & Timeline

For clarity:

- **June 2026** – Major Build announcements occurred, including IQ layers, MAI models, Agent Framework, HorizonDB, and governance tooling ([aguidetocloud.com](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/blog/microsoft-build-2026-recap/)).  
- **July 1, 2026** – Document PII NextGen Playground became generally available ([azurecharts.com](https://azurecharts.com/updates?service=6)).  
- **July 15, 2026 (today)** – Advanced platform metrics (preview) and DevUI Agent Inspector announced ([azurecharts.com](https://azurecharts.com/updates?monthback=0)).

---

###  What This Means for Developers & Enterprises

- **Developers** can now experiment freely with PII detection in ads or documents via the NextGen Playground. The Agent Framework improvements and contextual IQ layers facilitate richer, intelligent agent creation across Foundry, Copilot, and internal systems.
- **Organizations** planning AI deployment can leverage HorizonDB for performant, managed AI data workloads, and use governance layers like Agent 365 and ACS for compliance, auditing, and lifecycle control.
- **Security and DevOps** teams should update policies and tooling to include agent-aware practices—particularly around data access, identity, and behavioral observability, as highlighted in the Azure Database Security Newsletter ([techcommunity.microsoft.com](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/coreinfrastructureandsecurityblog/azure-database-security-newsletter---july-2026/4534477)).

---

###  For Further Reading

- Visit the **Azure Updates** portal for the most recent news (July 15 items) ([azure.microsoft.com](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/updates/)).  
- Review the **Microsoft Build 2026 Book of News** to trace availability timelines, feature statuses, and next steps ([aguidetocloud.com](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/blog/microsoft-build-2026-recap/)).  
- Explore **Azure Charts – Latest Azure AI Services updates** for a granular view of feature rollout statuses ([azurecharts.com](https://azurecharts.com/updates?service=6)).  
- Check out the **Azure Database Security Newsletter (July 2026)** for insights on securing AI-backed workflows ([techcommunity.microsoft.com](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/coreinfrastructureandsecurityblog/azure-database-security-newsletter---july-2026/4534477)).
